utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, you have a matter to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Very briefly. Yesterday, or last evening I should say, Ms. Residovic notified the Prosecution that Witness Popovski, who will be the witness after the next witness, had arrived in The Hague bringing several documents, which the Defence saw for the first time yesterday afternoon, and these documents may be used during the direct examination of the witness, we understand, or they may not be. Nevertheless, they were provided to the Prosecution last evening, However, of course, only in the Macedonian language in Cyrillic script. So, obviously, the Prosecution has not been able to review this new information with any great care. Having said that, Your Honour, we would like to propose that we go forward with our cross-examination today. We will do our very best to complete both cross-examinations. If it appears that there is some matter arising from one or more of these documents that would require some additional study or questioning, we might request that the witness Popovski be held over until Monday. But, like I said, we hope that will not happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. We call the first of the two witnesses. Did you need to say something, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just to confirm that everything which my learned colleague, Mr. Saxon, has said is correct. Yesterday, we received the materials. We handed it over to the Prosecution. We believe there are no substantial changes, but the witness established one mistake vis-a-vis his statement and this is why he brought in the material which confirms his final findings. The Defence believes that if the Prosecution deems it necessary, it needs more time for the cross-examination, that we will not object. And if the Trial Chamber holds its session on Friday, then this can be done on Friday; and then if not, then by Monday we can finish with the two witnesses. And as we promised, we would have finished by then with the presentation of all the statements of all our witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Is there any matter beyond the tendering of the statement you need to raise with the witness, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask that the set of documents be distributed at this time, in view of the fact that these questions will be related to the statement given in this 92 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can it be clear, Ms. Residovic, that the Chamber does not expect that you will examine this witness in chief because of the statement of evidence. If there is some change from the statement, that can be dealt with shortly; otherwise, do not proceed with an examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is quite clear to me, and I will ask questions of the witness only about the documents related to the statements which Defence wants, as the Chamber suggested, and wishes to tender into evidence in regards to the statement which the witness has made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Zdravkovski. Can you please tell us your full name and date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You no need to -- that is all proved by the witness, you see. The statement will be the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. If I followed, well, the 92 bis rule well, I would then ask -- I would ask that 65 ter document 1D124 [as interpreted] be shown to the witness. It is after tab 1; 65 ter 1D1248, after tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, have you ever been requested to give a statement by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in the ensuing period, was your statement verified by the officials of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, in January of this year.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at page 1D9953; English 1D9955. Mr. Zdravkovski, is this the statement which you gave to the Defence, later verified by the court officials?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the other page of your statement, which in the Macedonian is 1D9954. Is this your signature, Mr. Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we seek to tender this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is -- it has already been noted as 1D -- D125 MFI; and as we suggest, since this was a statement used during cross-examination, that this 65 ter statement be placed under number D125, so as to avoid confusion during the overview of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. The statement marked for identification will now become an exhibit with the same number, and the formally witnessed and signed copy will be used to replace the copy used for the original marked for identification exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That would be Exhibit 1D125, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, after having given the statement, did the Defence ask of you to submit certain documents?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I received a call from someone from the Ministry of Interior - I think it was the state secretary - who asked of me to submit copies of the criminal report because this was requested by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you to look at document after tab 3 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Exhibit 1D188, MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page number in the English version, 1D5348; and in the Macedonian, 1D5344.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Zdravkovski, what this document is?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: This document is communication from the MOI to the Defence that contains the number of criminal reports, the numbers under which they're registered and submitted to the public prosecutor's office in Bitola, and a list of persons, their names, first names and last names, persons against which such criminal reports were filed regarding the events in Bitola in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in view of the fact that the witness recognised the content of this document, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D188, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would now ask you, Mr. Zdravkovski, to look at document after tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1211.1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Branko Ristevski is?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: He is the head the SVR Bitola at the moment, and he came to position after -- after me. He followed me in this position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at the look after tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1211.2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The page is 1D9693.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see this document after tab 6?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here, it states: "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior, Bitola, sector of the interior, department for criminal police, section for general criminality?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: There is the number and the date of 14 June 2001, Bitola. Mr. Zdravkovski, do you know what this document is?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a copy of the criminal report of the 14th of June, 2001 filed by SVR Bitola to the public prosecutor's office in Bitola against 44 people in total, perpetrators of criminal deeds committed on the 30th of April, 2001-1st of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zdravkovski, even though we did warn you of the fact that you would have to wait for interpretation, this implies waiting for the interpretation for my questions. You really should speak freely and not make such pauses because your answers will be automatically interpreted. Therefore, if I understood you well, this is a criminal report which the sector which you headed filed against 44 persons regarding the event at the beginning of May; that is to say, on the 30th of April and the 1st of May, 2001. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. And I think there is also an event on the 1st -- on the night of 1st and 2nd of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at the document at tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1211.3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is a criminal report filed on the 19th of December, 2001 by SVR Bitola to the public prosecutor's office in Bitola against perpetrators of criminal acts relating to the events of 6th of June to the 7th of June, 2001. I believe there is also an event which moves or which is dated of the 7th to the 8th. All in all, 58 persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, at the moment when these criminal reports were filed, what was your position at the sector of the interior in Bitola?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I was the head of SVR Bitola.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, since the witness recognised this document, I seek to tender documents 1D1211.1, 1211.2, and 65 ter 1D1211.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1211.1 will become Exhibit 1D318; 65 ter 1D1211.2 will become Exhibit 1D319; and 65 ter 1D1211.3 will become Exhibit 1D320, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, please look at document after tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1239.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After having given the statement to the Defence which we've seen, were you asked to give any kind of information as to what happened to the criminal report?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I was asked by a representative from the MOI Skopje, I believe it was also the state secretary or one of his associates, regarding the further course of the criminal report in the judicial bodies.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you give this answer? Did you find out what happened to your criminal reports?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: In order to check this, I established contacts with the basic public prosecutor in Bitola; and from him, I received the statement from -- rescinding from Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You just mentioned that we are looking -- this is the statement you received. This is 65 ter 1D1239 from the March 15th. Is this the statement you were mentioning?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document after tab 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1240.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is page 1D1922 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, do you recognise this document and what is this document?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I recognise this document. This is the other statement on exemption on Prosecution regarding the second criminal report. The previous statement was regarding the first criminal report we looked, and this is a statement on exemption from the other criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why the public prosecutor did not the proceed with the prosecution with these persons?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Am I allowed to make one comment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I can see here, the second statement, the statement I'm looking at right now, pertains for the first criminal report. This is something I can see according to the dates, while the previous one pertains to the second criminal report which was filed later. My comment relates only to the order of these documents; otherwise, both these documents are authentic. This pertains to the exemption from prosecution by the prosecutor in Bitola and was sent to the Basic Court in Bitola to the investigating judge, since the procedure at that moment was in the investigation phase.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me why the prosecutor did not prosecute this case?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: According to what is said in the statement, and also according what the prosecutor told us in our conversation, the reason for the waiver from this prosecutor is the enforcement of the Law on Amnesty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender 65 ter 1D139 and 1D140 as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1D1239 will become Exhibit 1D321, and 65 ter 1D1240 will become Exhibit 1D322, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, do you know what the investigating judge did after the prosecutor waived prosecution?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: With regards to the same thing, I received this response from the prosecutor and a copy of the court document. The investigating court in Bitola, with regards to the first statement of the prosecutor, with regards to the first criminal report, and with regards to the second document act on waiving prosecution, with regards to the second criminal report, against a total of, I believe, 102 individuals, has passed decisions. So there were two separate decisions on terminating the investigation, on terminating the investigation procedure, that is, because of the reason that we mentioned already: The entry into force of the Law on Amnesty. And as I can see here, this took place on the 18th of March, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please look at the document after 10.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1241.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D22 -- 9924 in Macedonian version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's just wait until it shows on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the decision that you testified about before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you look now at the document in tab 11.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1242.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's wait until it is displayed. That is 1D9926. That is the Macedonian page.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do. This is the second decision of the Basic Court in Bitola of the investigating judge terminating the investigation procedure in relation to the second criminal report that deals with the events of June 2001, also because of the same reason, because of the entry into force of the Law on Amnesty. And as far as can I see, it was passed on the same date, this decision, on the 18th of March, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Zdravkovski, having in mind the Law on Amnesty, in which stage are the decisions made and who makes the decision on terminating the procedures or on the course and outcome of procedure pending?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: The decision on terminating the procedure pursuant to the Law on Amnesty could be passed in various stages of the procedure, depending on the stage that the procedure has reached. If it is a criminal report that has already been filed by the SVR and the case is in the hands of the public prosecutor, the prosecutor can terminate the procedure in that stage and invoke the Law on Amnesty. If the procedure is before the investigating judge, then the judge can terminate the investigation by passing a decision again invoking the Law on Amnesty, as it has been done in this case, also if, of course, upon a motion by the public prosecutor. But if the public prosecutor does not waive the prosecution, does not make such statement, then the criminal procedure has started before the court, then the court can bring the verdict, rejecting this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now look at the document in tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 65 ter 1D1305.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 1D0303. That is the Macedonian page, while 1D0352 is the page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, considering that we're speaking here about the decision of the appellate court in Skopje, is it possible to terminate the procedure also in the appeals procedure stage?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I said this could be done in all stages of the procedure, depending on the stage that the procedure has reached. As far as can I see, this is case before the appellate court in Skopje. That is the second instances in Republic of Macedonia. In this stage, the procedure was terminated by a decision. So it can be done in any stage of the procedure, also in the second instance procedure because the Law on Amnesty applies to any stage of the procedure might have reached.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I finally seek to tender, as Defence exhibits, the 65 ter document 1D1241, then 65 ter 1D1242; and then 65 ter 1D1305 is added to the 65 ter list of Defence exhibits and that it is received into evidence. And I have just one more question of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, assigned numbers are Exhibit 1D323, Exhibit 1D324, and Exhibit 1D325, respectfully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, with regards to the events that you described in your statement to the Defence, and because of which you filed the criminal reports that this Chamber has received into evidence, tell me whether the police of the sector of internal affairs that you headed has at any moment during those events participated on the side of the protesters, has it overstepped its powers, and has it in any way influenced the crowd to perpetrate criminal offences?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. This is ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If someone would assert something of that nature before this Chamber, before this Court, what would you say to this?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is completely untrue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the transcript, I indicate the transcript pages 2967, 2921, 2971, 2921 [as interpreted], 2922, then 2941, 2942, 2943, then 3199, then 3234, 3235, and, finally, 3248. And with regards to another witness, 58100 [as interpreted], 5825, and 5916. I have completed my examination, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I have no questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zdravkovski. My name is Gerard Dobbyn. I'm representing the Office of the Prosecutor in this case. And following on from my colleague, Ms. Residovic, I'm going to ask be asking you a few questions about your statement and the events that took place in Bitola. Now, Mr. Zdravkovski, as you explained, the riots in Bitola took place on two separate occasions. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the first occasion was in May, and the second time was in June of 2001. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: If you wish me to state the exact dates, the first one started in the evening of the 30th of April, 2001, after 2000 hours, and they lasted for several hours, until the early morning of 1st of May, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: After that, after that, if you allow me --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, actually, if you could just confirm that the second riots took place in June 2001, and that would be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: The second riots took place on the 6th, in the evening, 2001, and until the early morning of the 7th of June. And, on the 8th of June, the situation was again calm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And as a result of these riots, there was significant damage and destruction in Bitola, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: As a result of the riot, there was damage to property, to some 122 facilities, business, and housing facilities. That was the damage, property damage; however, I am happy, I was and I still am happy, that there were no casualties, human casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would you agree, Mr. Zdravkovski, that in Bitola at that time the public law and order was disturbed?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The publicity law and order was disturbed to a greater extent. This is how it is defined in the regulations that the Ministry of Interior follows, and this is it why we had analysed this situation seriously in the context of the conflict in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001. And the first task that my associates set for ourselves was to prevent the conflict from transferring to the area that I was the head of, because the operational information spoke that there was such realistic risk. And to prevent this from happening, my assessment was that we couldn't allow for a single casualty, even, because the experiences from the Balkan region, especially those in Bosnia-Herzegovina, say that even one human casualty would be sufficient to instigate an interethnic conflict with consequences that can't even be forecasted. And this is why we, acting in pursuant to the Law on Interior according to which we are in charge of protecting the lives of citizens, their personal safety and their property, in this order, we assumed the human lives as the priority value.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zdravkovksi. Thank you. I appreciate your answer. However, if at all possible, I would like you to keep your answers as brief as you could. Obviously, if you do need to explain certain matters, you are free to. But where a simple "yes" or "no" suffices, then that is what I would ask for? Now, after the first riots in May, isn't it true that a curfew was imposed on the town of Bitola?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: After the events of 1st of May, 2001, I, and the head of the service for state security in Bitola, have made a joint motion to introduce a curfew or restriction of movement of citizens. On the same date, 2nd of May, that was accepted by the then-minister of the interior. I believe that Dosta Dimovska was the minister then. We did this. Prosecutor, sir, I'm sorry, but I need to elaborate, so that I'm clear. We did this because in the context of my previous answer, our assessment was that this would be the best measure to achieve the end that we set, to prevent from -- to prevent a new conflict area in Macedonia from happening. And I believe you will agree as well that this is the priority objective, and this Chamber, I believe, will agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, despite the curfew, isn't it the case that the police were not able to prevent substantial damage and destruction to buildings in the second set of riots in June?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: The curfew, I said, was introduced on the second of May, 2001, and its impact was successful. On the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th of May, there were no unrest, riots. The curfew was mainly respected by the citizens. On the 20th of May, 2001, because the situation was stabilized, the curfew was abolished. So at the moment that the second riots took place, 6th of June, 2001, in Bitola there has been no curfew, but it was re-established again on the 6th, immediately when the events took place at 2000 hours. Because learning -- having learned from the previous experience that the curfew was an efficient measure on the evening of the 6th of June, I immediately filed a motion to introduce a curfew, and I believe that Mr. Boskoski was the minister then. He immediately accepted this; and at 2300 hours, on that same date, he issued the order to introduce the curfew, which was in force until the 6th of July, 2001, when the situation became fully calm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I just want it ask you, were you aware that there were allegations that, during the riots, members of the police force did nothing to stop the rioters destroying the ethnic Albanian property? I'm just asking whether you were aware of these allegations.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: That is absolutely untrue. Since we said -- I said in my statement that there was property damage, there were no attacks on Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the truth of these allegations at this time. I'm asking whether you were aware that these allegations were made.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: No. Nothing of the sort took place. There were no Albanians attacked. There were no human casualties, and no one was injured. No Albanian were injured. Maybe somebody who is objecting the work of the police minded this, found this hard to accept. I'm happy that there have been no casualties or victims. I am happy then and now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, I'd ask you to listen to the question and answer the question, and my question was: Were you aware that allegations had been made that police took part in these riots.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I believe that I stated clearly. I had no such information, and something of the sort was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. So would it be fair to say that also you were not aware of allegations that, as well as not stopping rioters from destroying property, police actively took part in these riots themselves?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: That is an absolute untruth. The police officers, with regard to the protests, participated on the side of the police, with the professional and police dignity, and within the competencies that they have pursuant to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zdravkovski, can I ask you to turn to tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry. We have binders to distribute at this time. Sorry, I should do that first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zdravkovski, can you turn to tab 5, please. And what you have in front of you, this is 65 ter number 1191, is an article by Colleen Barry of the Associated Press, and it is dated 2 July 2001. It's headed, Paramilitary Threat Emerges in Macedonian Conflict. Do you see that, Mr. Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, if you could please turn to the second page, it's about two thirds of the way down in the Macedonian version, halfway in the English. There's a paragraph starting, "Following a pattern ... Have you located that paragraph? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you will see that this states: "Following a pattern, some fear will spread to Skopje and other cities. Western and government sources say police officers were among gangs that destroyed Albanian businesses and targeted the homes of prominent Albanians in Bitola in May after four policemen from the southern city died in the conflict." Do you see that, Mr. Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I see it. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, do you go that, according to this article, the information that some police officers took part in the rioting was actually provided by Macedonian government sources? Would you agree that this is what the article states? That just calls for a "yes" or "no" answer, Mr. Zdravkovski. It's in front of you on the page.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Which question do you want me to answer by "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I want you to answer the question I just asked, which is: Do you see that, according to this article, the information that police officers took part in the rioting was provided by Macedonian government sources? Isn't that what it says in the article here?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: First, I have an objection, and I can't answer this question "yes" or "no" because I heard your entire question. And Prosecutor, sir, and, Your Honours, I believe that I need it elaborate on this, if you allow me, because parts of your questions were factually inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we will proceed most quickly if you listen to the question that is asked of you and answer that question, not seek to answer something else or justify what you think is right about the question. So could you listen to Mr. Dobbyn's precise question and answer that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And my question, Mr. Zdravkovski, is: Do you see that, according to this article, the information that police took part in the riots in Bitola came from Macedonian government sources?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I see it. That's an article.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, so, your testimony is that, even though according to this article government sources in Skopje had this information, you, as of the head of the police in Bitola, did not. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: What I see here is a journalist's article, and this is a free journalist interpretation. I don't consider this a relevant fact. This is just an opinion of someone that something allegedly came from governmental sources, but, factually, this is inaccurate, as it is also inaccurate that there were police officers killed in May. That is something that was important, and the police officers were killed on the 28th of May. If someone who wrote this article, this one that we have here, has made a mistake with regard to the date of killing of the police officers, this is an evidence of how responsible he was in compiling his journalist report, because he wrote this two months after the events, and I'm now speaking seven years after the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honours, I would seek to tender this article, which is 65 ter 1191.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is the evidentiary value of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: The evidentiary value, Your Honour, goes to the knowledge that was in the community about the allegations, not necessarily to the truth of the allegations, themselves, but just that there was information in the media that these allegations were being made, and the impact this would have on whether an investigation should be taken into these allegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that was in Macedonian media?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that this particular one was, but it goes to the sources that the information supposedly came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We don't receive this article, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I would, then, just ask that it be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P583, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, can you now please turn to tab 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P329. It's a Human Rights Watch Report dated 6 June 2001. It is entitled: Macedonia rioters burn Albanian homes in Bitola. Police fail to stop violence. Some actively participate. So do you see, Mr. Zdravkovski, that Human Rights Watch also appear to have received information that police officers from Bitola took part in the rioting? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I see it; however, it is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, can I now ask you to turn to the second page, Mr. Zdravkovski.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, actually -- sorry. This will be on the -- no, it is the second page. There's an article, a paragraph, approximately half way down, starting, "Human Rights Watch called ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And it states: "Human Rights Watch called on the Macedonian Ministry of Interior to carry out an immediate investigation into the conduct of the Bitola police during the riots and urged the international community to assist and participate in the investigation." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Zdravkovski, isn't it also true that these allegations of police involvement in the riots were also reported on by Macedonian media?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: There was speculations, I call them speculations, in there various media, especially during such periods of conflict. You have several speculations within one day. This is the job of the media to present sensation so they have wider circulation or audience. These are just speculations. The Bitola police, I claim with full responsibility, is one of the most responsible and most professional sectors in the state and beyond.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So can I take it that earlier on, when you told me that you had no knowledge of any allegations about police misconduct during the riots, you were actually aware that such allegations existed in the Macedonian media?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I said the allegations that we see now, coming from both the foreign and the domestic media, these are just journalists' articles. I don't consider them facts. When the first events took place in Bitola, for instance, at 2000 hours, the police general, then Mr. Galevski, arrived and he was personally present at every check-point where the events took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, I believe you have gone past the scope of the question, which was again simple was: You were aware that these allegations were being made in the media, correct?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: The media can write anything. I don't consider that facts. When mentioning the general, I meant to say that we had already had, even before it was requested by Human Rights Watch, we had a super control by the police general. He came to the spot and his assessment was that we had the optimum procedures, and the result is the evidence of this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Was General Galevski present at every check-point?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: General Galevski, during the first event, those on the -- in the night between 30th April to 1st of May 2001, he then came at 2000 hours; and until the end of events, he was present in Bitola. He visited all check-points, together with the then-head of the police department in the SVR Bitola, and they made suggestions with regards to interventions. And with his vast experience, I believe that he helped us avoid casualties and preventing the threat of creating the second conflict focus in the state, because Bitola is specific -- a historically and culturally specific city of importance for the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, when you say he made suggestions, were these suggestions followed?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He was a general in the police, and I think he was of key assistance for having avoided more serious consequences. And if you allow me, I would also mention some conversations between him and myself at those moments. They have just come to my mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think that goes to the question that I asked you, so I don't need to hear it at this point. But can I ask you to turn your mind back to the report from Human Rights Watch that I showed you just a moment ago; and in that report, Human Rights Watch urged the Ministry of Interior to investigate the conduct of the Bitola police. Now, did you ever receive any instructions from your superiors in the ministry in Skopje to investigate these allegations?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: The word "investigation," to me, has a criminal and a legal connotations. We don't carry these investigations within the ministry. This is done by the investigating judge according to the rules and regulations in Macedonia. This is why I don't understand what you mean by "investigation."

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. Did you receive any instructions from your superiors in Skopje to make inquiries into the truth of these allegations.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I mentioned that, for the first event and for the second event also, maybe once or twice I was in contact with the ministers of interior at the time and with the director of internal affairs. And you can see through the documents that, after the first event and after the second events, the measure curfew was immediately undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovksi, please. I am sorry to interrupt, but it is very important that you listen to the question and you answer the question that I'm asking you. The question I've asked you is whether you received instructions from the Ministry of Interior to make inquiries about the allegations that police had participated in the riots. That's the question, and I would like you to answer that question and that question alone.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I do not recall of such activities because it was evident, very evident, that this has not happened, and that these were just speculations on the part of journalists. You can see that I really do not want to comment any of this. These are clear and mere speculations because the general was on the ground and would have suggested it if he had found anything of this kind happening. There was just proper action on the part of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll move on to a slightly different topic. In your statement, you've described various operative measures and activities that SVR Bitola undertook in relation to the riots, and one of the measures you described, for example, was imposing curfews. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, at this point, I'd ask you to turn to tab 9 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 1D940. It's an obligatory instruction from the Republic secretariat of internal affairs from 1976, and a portion of this has been admitted earlier as Exhibit 1D311.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I would ask you to turn to item 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: This is on page 28 in the Macedonian. In e-court, it's ERN 1D00-8140. And in the English, it's page 12, which is 1D00-8167.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you have item 44 in front of you, Mr. Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And above item 44, do you see the heading: Operative action?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And that states: "The public security service organises operative action for the purpose of conducting specific tasks which require extended, coordinated, synchronised, and time-limited engagement of the service particularly with regards to ..." And then lists certain actions. And if you carry on down, you'll see it lists "public law and order." Do you see that, Mr. Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I see it and I know this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, so, would you agree that the actions that were taken in Bitola, including the imposition of a curfew, would appear to fit within this definition of "operative action"?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zdravkovski, doesn't this say here that operative actions, one of the purposes for them, is to maintain the public law and order? Is that right? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I see this here. However, according to our police work, the notion "operative action" means something altogether and is not correlated with the activities in each specific disturbance of the public law and order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, I'm asking you to look at this particular document from 1976 and this particular definition of "operative action," and would you agree that the actions that were undertaken in Bitola would fit in with this particular definition of "operative action"?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Operation action -- operative activities, yes; but operative action, no. This is altogether different. This is carried out based on previous information about an event, protection of political persons events, and so forth. In this case, we had unexpected events --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Zdravkovski --

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: -- which caused emotional reactions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I must interrupt again, because you're not answering my question. In front of you, you have a definition of "operative action." I'm not asking you about the definition that you used in 2001. I'm asking you about this definition in front of you. Don't the actions that you did take in 2001 fit in with this particular definition of "operative action"?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps, because of differences in legal systems, we're unable to understand each other. Operative action is a formal type of action previously established regarding certain activities which the police has to undertake. In this case, we had an unexpected disturbance of the public law and order which caused emotional reactions of the young population of Bitola, which in turn came as a result of other activities or events that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, can I just ask you, then: Was the decision to impose a curfew, was that done to ensure the public safety and public law and order?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, in order to restore security in the city and to ensure the lives and personal safety of the people, and then property, their property, to calm the situation down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I would seek to tender 65 ter 1D940.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P584, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And you've also testified, haven't you, or at least it's contained within your statement, that the decisions to issue the curfew, the orders, were, in fact, issued first of all by the previous minister of the interior, Dosta Dimovska, and later on by the -- the later minister, Ljube Boskoski? Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So would you agree that these orders which had been made to protect the public law and order were being issued directly by the ministers?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is their authorisation given by law. Upon the proposal of the head of the SVR, This decision is issued by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And during your testimony earlier on, a number of documents were admitted relating to charges against people arising from the riots. And we saw that there were initially 44 people were charged in relation to the earlier riots and 58 in relation to the later riots. Would it be fair to say, Mr. Zdravkovski, that among those 102 persons, there were no charges laid against any police officers from Bitola?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: There would have been if there were grounded suspicions that an authorised official has committed a criminal act. In order to submit a criminal report, be it a civilian or an authorised official, there needs to be grounded suspicions that that person has committed a criminal act. In this case, this did not happen. As I said, these were just speculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Did you make any inquiries at all into these speculations?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. The work of the police of the heads in the police is to check everything they hear about. Everything has been checked. Everything is clean. I'm very pleased with all authorised officials and how they acted, which as well as others from other SVRs who came to assist us, and I congratulate them now also for not allowing Bitola to become the second conflict focus and to preserve its cosmopolitan spirit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So should I take it from this that when you earlier said that you had no knowledge of any allegations against police officers being engaged in the riots in Bitola, what you actually meant to say was, yes, you did have knowledge of this, and, yes, you did make inquiries, but, no, you didn't find anything had taken place. Is that what you're now saying?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I said that, at that time, the newspapers and the media disseminated such speculations. I did not say I had nod heard them. Also the public prosecutor in Bitola has charged a deputy who follows all speculations in all media on a daily basis, and he always asks all of us to check them, and he himself can initiate criminal reports against official -- authorised officials if there is any truth in such speculation. This means that, had there been such cases, the public prosecutors would have acted. Nothing of this kind happened; therefore, there was no action.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So because this was in the media, are you saying you left it to the public prosecutor to decide whether any action should be taken?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: According to my authorisations, competencies, but also in view of my nature as manager in the police, I had daily contacts with the prosecutor. So, therefore, my answer is the same as that of the prosecutor. We worked together on a daily basis, and our joint conclusion was that all of these are but empty speculations, which is to be expected under the circumstances such as we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: What specific inquiries to did you make to establish that these were simply speculations?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I will now tell you something which, until now, I refrained from saying, because I esteem your time and the time of the Trial Chamber, but I have to say this now. The head of the SVR in Bitola who undertakes measures, in cooperation with subordinates, has to take into account, to remain within the frames of the law, and, at the same time, to respect human rights, including the right to demonstrations, spontaneous, without announcements. Third, but not least, in importance, perhaps the most important thing is that care has to be given to the possible consequences of these events. The character of the consequences told me --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt you, Mr. Zdravkovski, but from what I'm seeing so for, this doesn't appear to be answering my question at all. My question was simply: Specifically, what inquiries did you make into the allegations of misconduct by the police. I want you to answer that. I want you to tell me specifically what you did to verify these allegations.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: At all check-points, I had a senior official, and I immediately received information about the situation there. I believed these senior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the second set of charges against the 58 individuals for the riots in June were presented to the public prosecutor on 19th of December, 2001. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There is what is written in the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that in the months leading up to December, after the signing of the Ohrid Agreement, at that time it was well known that a Law on Amnesty in was going to be coming into effect?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I would not know. I'm not a politician.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So are you saying that you had absolutely no knowledge about a discussion on a Law on Amnesty?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't recall anything of this kind. I believe the priority then was to calm down the situation, and this was, in fact, the purpose of the Ohrid Framework Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, specifically, relating to the Law on Amnesty, isn't it the case, Mr. Zdravkovski, that the amnesty law applies to criminal proceedings, not disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. You said whether this was correct. Is it not true or is it true? My answer is, yes, this is true. It pertains to criminal proceedings, not disciplinary proceedings. The Law on Amnesty pertains only to criminal responsibility and accountability, not disciplinary accountability. This is something done within the ministry. I made a problem -- a proposal -- I make the proposal for disciplinary accountability. The minister makes the decision. This is something altogether different.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And I understand that you testified earlier on that decisions on whether cases -- sorry, whether the amnesty law will be applied to particular cases is in the hands either of the public prosecutor or the judge. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I said that the amnesty law can be applied by the prosecutor, the first instance court, the Court of Appeals, depending -- the phase -- depending on the phase of the procedure. I think I was clear in explaining this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, you were. And would you agree that the amnesty law does not state that the police can make decisions on whether the amnesty will apply to particular cases?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: For the -- I was not competent for the enforcement of the amnesty law. I have not analysed this. This is the work of the judicial system. My work is to submit and to file a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And after you submitted and filed a criminal report, it was then for the public prosecutor and/or the judge to decide whether the amnesty law applied. Correct?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, if you could please turn to tab 24 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: This is 65 ter number 1D168. This is a document from the government of the Macedonia entitled: Reasons for passing of the law, referring to the Law on Amnesty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Do you have that document in front of you, Mr. Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Not yet. Now I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay. And if you look at the second paragraph, it states: "The motives of passing of this law are also included in the statement of the president of the Republic of Macedonia," and it carries on "regarding the need for reintegration in the democratic society of the persons that have prepared and participated in the actions relating to the conflict in the Republic of Macedonia by 26/9/2001 and their integration in the normal course of life." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Would you agree, from what it says there, the purpose of this law was to reintegrate people back into Macedonian society and specifically NLA members?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Whereby, here it is not stated members of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: But that's your understanding of the reason behind the law.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: This is not how I understand it. Perhaps, this is how you understand it. Here it reads, "persons." This means all citizens of the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, do you see where it refers to the statement of the president of the Republic of Macedonia given to senior members of the European Union, NATO, and OSCE? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: In the upper part?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, then, if you could please turn to tab 24 of your binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 1D193.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Zdravkovski, unfortunately, we do not have a Macedonian version of this letter. It's very short. I will read it to you in English, and it will be translated as I read. This is a letter from the president of the Republic of Macedonia to Lord Robertson, the Secretary-General of NATO, and dated 13 August 2001. It states: "I hereby confirm that the NLA will be able to benefit from the opportunities offered by the government for reintegrating into society in accordance with my plan and programme for overcoming the crisis." Did you follow that, Mr. Zdravkovski?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And, just for the record, I'm not sure if I put it on, it's Exhibit 1D193.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now going back, again, to tab 25 to the reasons for passing of the law. Do you see, then, that the reference to the reasons given in the letter to NATO refers to reintegrating members of the NLA into society?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Now, if you could turn to page 3 of the document, you will see a heading at the top of the page: Explanatory notes. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And the second paragraph, under Roman numeral II: "The president of the state issued a declaration and the government supported it, where he underlined the determination of the president and the government to grant amnesty to the NLA members." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: So, again, this emphasises, doesn't it, that the amnesty was intended to benefit the members of the NLA?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And if you look at Roman numeral III, headed, Objectives that are to be achieved with the law, it states under that: "The amnesty law covers persons that have participated in the conflict and which have voluntarily given up weapons by 26/9/2001, as well as persons against which this are ongoing and pre-criminal and criminal proceedings." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And where it refers to persons who voluntarily gave up weapons on 26/9/2001, who gave up their weapons on that date?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't think this is a question for me. I cannot speak about things which are outside the territorial jurisdiction of SVR Bitola. Even if I were to attempt to give you an answer, I would speculate; and as you have already been able to hear, I don't take much to speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well, would you agree that, to your knowledge, there were no police or other security force members handing in weapons on that date?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I said I don't feel competent to say anything about this. A witness is supposed to speak of facts, and I declare that I would speak the truth and nothing but the truth. And I'm a witness not for the Prosecution or the Defence; I'm a witness for the truth. Therefore, I would please ask you not to ask me questions which I don't feel competent to respond to. I don't see myself as a journalist, but really as a witness. I would really not want to speculate. First of all, it's been seven years --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. If I can just ask you, then, you were the head of SVR Bitola at that time. Were any of the police officers in Bitola handing in weapons to the government on 26 September 2001?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I don't understand. Why would the police hand over their weapons? They are authorised officials. They have weapons to this day. They're -- prior to the conflict, during the conflict, and after the conflict, they had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you have answered my question there. If I could just follow that up: What was the purpose of operation Essential Harvest?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Again, this is a question outside the scope of my competency. But if you allow me, I could recall something about this. The information from the media stated that this was to collect illegal arms and weapons and ammunition from the area engulfed by the conflict. I believe this was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: This was an action on the part of the international community to collect illegal weapons, weapons held without permits --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: -- and I believe this action yielded in some minimal results.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I have just a few propositions that I would like to put to you. I would simply like you to indicate whether you agree or not with these propositions, and I would try to keep this as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And before I get to that, Your Honour, I would seek to tender 65 ter 1D168.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P585, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, do you agree that during the riots in Bitola, the response of the police was inadequate, some police refused to intervene, and some police even took part in the riots. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Absolutely no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Would you agree that these allegations against the police were widely reported and widely known in Macedonia at the time?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I said already, there were such speculations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Would you agree that of the people charged in relation to the riots in Bitola, none were police officers?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. There was no one charged because the police were carrying out their police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would you agree that no police officers were internally disciplined for participating in the riots?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: They could not be subject to disciplinary proceedings because none took part in anything of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And would you agree that there was no real investigation or inquiry into these allegations against police officers?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, Your Honours, I don't think whether you can understand me. The -- what the police did was to such an extent optimal and proper, if they had to do it all over again, they would do it again or we would do it again in the same way. We prevented a conflict from breaking out. I am proud to have had such police officers. Bitola is a cosmopolitan city, then and now. After the conflict, we had a social activity to restore interethnic trust. I was one of the participants in this, and it was a success. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovksi, sorry to interrupt--

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: -- we live again together.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, but I will take that as a "no." My final question for you, Mr. Zdravkovski, is: Isn't it true that these allegations were not investigated because at that time within the Ministry of Interior, there was no will amongst the leadership to investigate or discipline employees of the MOI for offences committed against ethnic Albanians in the course of the conflict in 2001. Do you agree with that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, Your Honours, really, if you continue to ask me questions of this kind, I am libel to think that someone would want conflict and lives to fall again in my country. We prevented this from happening, and I am proud to have done this. The cosmopolitan spirit of Bitola continues to live on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor, following our required procedures, is putting to certain propositions. It's self-evident from the general tenor of your evidence that you will not agree about almost all of them. In fact, perhaps, there is only one that you would have any agreement with. But all he needs from you is confirmation whether you agree or don't agree with the proposition. You are not, unnaturally, but not within the needs of our procedures, trying to answer the truth of the substance of the proposition all over again. You don't need to do that; simply say whether you agree are disagree. And I would anticipate, I think without any fear of contradiction, that you do not agree with this last proposition.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours. My deep apologies, but I'm not a professional witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you confirm that you don't agree with that last proposition; that is, that there was no investigation and no --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Dobbyn.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Thank you for your time, Mr. Zdravkovski, and that is the end of my questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have the first break now and resume earlier than normal, at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Zdravkovski, my learned friend, the Prosecutor, showed you a document, and you stated that you haven't seen that newspapers Fakti. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: A provision was quoted saying that some governmental sources alleged the police was involved in the events. Tell me, please, have you ever heard any government source saying anything of that sort?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Not directly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you were asked about the operative action, you explained that it is introduced in the police with regards to some expected events, and you then said that you undertook some operative actions [as interpreted]. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Operative activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in addition to this activity that was undertaken by means of introducing the curfew, could you tell us about any other operative activities that the police of the SVR Bitola undertook at that time?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: We continuously undertook other activities in cooperation also with the state security service. Involved were also members of the crime police, plain clothes police, who, within their competencies, worked on prevention and undertook activities for the entire duration of the curfew, 24 hours a day. The leadership, headed by me, has established contacts with the families of many individuals which we believed would be of key importance, so that through them we could achieve the impact and that would be for the demonstrations to stop the immediate next day. And if you count the hours, you will notice that we just had several hours on the first day; and on the second day, the situation was calm. This was as a result of those activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Tell me, please, in this operative activities, because of the first and second round of events, did you contact the injured persons, the injured parties?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I contacted the injured, the aggrieved persons, of course those that I could establish contact with, throughout the events, immediately when the events commenced, during the actual events taking place, and after the events. And this is how we achieved this impact that there was not a single casualty.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During these contacts with the aggrieved persons, was any of the aggrieved persons or any other citizen complaining of the police conduct or reported any police officer as being in misconduct?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Nothing of the sort happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Answering the questions of my learned friend, you said that you trusted your subordinated officers.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, with regards to these rumours in the public, that the police officers were in misconduct or participated in the riots, have you ever discussed those with your subordinated officers, that would be the heads of departments, OVRs, or commanders of the police stations?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I had continuous discussions with my subordinated officers, and our conclusion was that these were just empty speculations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your superior -- subordinated officers see with their own eyes any police officer in misconduct, overstepping the powers?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were your subordinated officers reported by anyone, any police officer as having done something unlawful?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that the area was visited by General Risto Galevski during the first event. Do you remember having said this?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I remember Risto Galevski arrived around 2000 hours immediately when the event started.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, with regards to the events, who from the SVR Bitola made the decisions?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I, together with my associates, since the head of the SVR is always and exclusively responsible for undertaking of the operative activities. This is what the law provides.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you strong enough or did you have enough strength to be on top of such massive unrest and riots?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: If you are referring to the number of police forces in the SVR Bitola, we did not have enough officers because after four were killed on the 28th of April, the entire unit of police Bitola, which was on the grounds together with those who were killed, was given a leave for one month, and this unit did not participate. This is I why we needed reinforcement. In contact with Mr. Galevski, we were provided such reinforcements throughout the time, and we were assisted by several SVRs. I can mention some of those, as far as I remember: Prilep, Ohrid, Gevgelija, Strumica, Velis. Maybe I made some mistakes, but I have forgotten something, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You stated that, as soon as the riots started, you made the proposal, and the that minister, Dosta Dimovska, and in June it was the Minister Ljube Boskoski, gave the order to introduce the curfew pursuant to their legal competencies. Was that your answer given to my learned friend?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. That was done on my proposal, since under the law, it is I, as head of the SVR, who is making the proposal, and the minister has the legal authority to order curfew. This is one of the rare --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Please, if have you the Prosecutor's binder, could you turn to tab number 25.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is P86, Law on Internal Affairs, and that is the Article 30.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is this the legal provision according to which the minister can order closing access to a certain facility or area or prohibition to leave the facility or the area without authorisation?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. But the grounds for this order, I believe, can be seen in the order itself, if you have it, because it indicates also other legal basis for the order. But this is one of the articles on the basis in which it says, in paragraph 2 of Article 30, that the measures of Article -- of paragraph 1 of this Article can be ordered by a minister or an officially authorised by him. What does this mean? That this law gives authority to the minister to undertake this because the minister can undertake such activities only when authorised by the law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Asked by my learned colleague, you stated that the Essential Harvest Operation that the international community was in charge of and that you have heard about from the media meant collecting weapons in illegal possession. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it any difference made whether it was weapons in illegal possessions or Macedonian, Albanians, Turks, Roma, or others; or was it that the total amount of illegal weapons were to be collected?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I can answer this with competence. The request pertained to all citizens of the Republic of Macedonia; and in SVR Bitola, we also had collection points where Macedonians, Turks, Vlachs, Roma, and all other citizens of the Republic of Macedonia brought weapons, those that were residing on the territory of SVR Bitola.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned colleague asked you several questions related to the application of the Law on Amnesty. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
