utterances.text: And tell me, please, what is applicable in the Republic of Macedonia, the law or the elaborations the rational accompanying this law which are submitted to the parliament before the law is passed?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: The law. There is no dilemma. The law is the applicable instrument.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will kindly ask that the witness is shown again P585. That is N005-1592. It used to be 1D1933, the page that is the item 3 on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend showed you part of the introductory remarks related to the passing of the law, and I will show this paragraph 3 which means -- aims to be achieved through the legislation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not here. The page is 1D1933.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see it? Chapter 3?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The title says: The aims that need to be achieved through the law. Would you kindly look at paragraph 2 which reads: "Namely, Article 1 sets forth the basis that the amnesty applies to the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, persons with legal residence, or persons who have property or family in the Republic of Macedonia, who, during the conflict of 2001, ending with 26th of September, 2001, have perpetrated criminal offences sanctioned under the Criminal Code and other laws of the Republic of Macedonia." When these objectives are described, Mr. Zdravkovski, do you see any distinction made between the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia based on any ground?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: I see no difference, and I see that I stated this already in my answer to the Prosecutor. In the second line of the second paragraph, it is stated the citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, and I believe this is clear for everyone. And I stated that in the practice in Bitola, were handed over weapons by many citizens of the Republic of Macedonia of all nationalities, those who wanted to hand the weapons over.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I kindly ask that the witness is now shown Exhibit 1D325, page 1D0340; the English, 1D0352.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You remember that earlier this morning, we discussed that the procedure could be terminated in any stage of the procedure, and you recognised this as being the termination of the procedure on the grounds of the amnesty law during the appeals procedure. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you to turn to page 2 of this decision of the appellate court in Skopje. I apologise. You don't have our binder here. You had it this morning. But maybe can you follow it from the display, so that we don't waste time.

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. I am able, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The final paragraph of the Macedonian text has this second sentence: "Namely, pursuant to the indicated legal basis, freed of prosecution are and the criminal proceedings are terminated and completely exempt from serving the sentence are citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, persons with legal residence, as well as persons who have property or family in the Republic of Macedonia, regarding which there has been a reasonable doubt that they have been preparing or participating in criminal offences related to the conflict in 2001, ending with the 26th of September, 2001." Mr. Zdravkovski, is this position of the appellate court in Skopje in correspond to your position, that the law applies to all citizens?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Absolutely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will kindly ask you now to look at the third page of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is 1D0342, and the English is 1D0354. And if we could look now at the second sentence in the rationale given by the appeals chamber, it reads: "Mainly, as can be seen from the documents of the case file, the content of the indictment and the evidence attached to it, it stems that the criminal -- criminal law event happened on 2nd September, 2001, when the accused, in the capacity of a conscript in the reserve composition of the Republic of Macedonia security forces, in the ranks of a police patrol on the Tetovo-Skopje highway, at the control security check-point opposite the petrol station Seven Brothers, never village Semeniste, Skopje was assigned when conducting official activity-check and inspection of the vehicles and persons whereby he was issued with weapon. "The aforementioned circumstances related to the time-frame of the event, time, and circumstances, as well as the capacity of the accused and the type of official tasks that he performed point to the fact that the criminal event is related to the conflict in the Republic of Macedonia in 2001."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, does this stance of the appellate court in Skopje correspond to your evidence before this Court, that the Law on Amnesty applied to all citizens of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: KRISTO ZDRAVKOVSKI
utterances.text: Absolutely. It corroborates it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Zdravkovski, you will be pleased to know that that concludes your questioning. We would thank you for your attendance in The Hague. The court officer will now show you from the court and you may return to your normal activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, or whoever is appropriate, for the next witness, we would have at this moment at the most only 20 minutes remaining. Is there any prospect of finishing the witness in that time, assuming five minutes only is spent by Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, that is just not realistic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. To speed up proceedings, I think we might have the witness called and the statement tendered, so that we're ready for cross-examination on Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just so you know, Your Honours, Ms. Valabhji will be dealing with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Would you please take the card that is given to you and read aloud the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Popovski. My name is Edina Ms. Residovic, and together with my colleague, Guenael Mettraux, I am the Defence counsel for Mr. Ljube Boskoski. You already know this, but I'm saying this for the purpose of the transcript. Please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: My name is Popovski, Gjoko.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovski, what is your profession?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: I am a graduate from the Faculty of Law.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is your work position today?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Today, I'm, at the work post, assistant minister in the sector for material, financial, technical, and logistic affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since when have you been employed at the MOI?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: I have been employed at the MOI since the 15th of March, 2007, first as advisor in the property section at the sector for material, financial, technical, and logistic affairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, before I proceed with my questions, I would ask that the witness, the Court, and my colleagues be given some of the documents which I would like to tender together with the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovski, did you -- at any point of time, were you asked to look at the facts or to check the facts given by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. Sometime in July, there was a request made by Mr. Dragan Godzo, authorised by the Defence of Mr. Boskoski, to check a list of 40 members of the reserve forces who, if any, were and whether they were engaged as reservists and whether any of them drew their salary or was employed at the ministry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic, could I, once again, please, indicate that this should not be taken as an opportunity to go over the evidence again of the witness which is contained in the statement. All of that matter that you've dealt with to date is already in the statement. If there are particular documents to which you want the witness to refer, you may go straight to them and deal with them. We're very concerned, with the last witness, you took 55 minutes of the hour we are allocated to that witness. This is a Rule 92 bis witness, the statement is admitted on your motion, the witness is here for cross-examination. So we want you to be just to the point of any particular matter that needs clarifying or any particular document that needs admitting, and then the rest of the time is for the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. At the onset of today, I mentioned that there were some changes, and this is the reason -- the only reason why I had to ask the witness the previous question; otherwise, I am fully aware of your instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovski, could you please look at the document after tab 3.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the document which you received and which you testified about in your statement?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document behind tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first document was 65 ter 1D1308, and this is document 1D13 -- 65 ter 1D1309.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the document which you issued?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document which I issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovski, when you were informed that you would be coming to this Tribunal to be cross-examined, did you undertake any kind of additional measures to, once again, establish the accuracy of the data which you provided in this document and in your statement?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. When I was informed that I would be coming to the Tribunal, I undertook additional measures to verify the list, to check the list. The previous checks were of the payroll of the ministry; and since none of these persons were on the payroll, this meant that none of them was in regular employment with the ministry. After the checks from -- received from the SVR, because in this specific case SVR Skopje is responsible for this area, it was evident that eight of these persons at a given period of time were given some kind of compensations; that is to say, they were engaged. When I was called in to come here, I made some additional checks, and I was able to see that an omission was made in the list -- in the previously submitted list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What kind of omission was this? Can you tell this Court?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is an omission of six persons of which two specifically represent a classic omission: Sladinovksi Zoran and Sekerovksi Borce; and the second admission was that they were wrongly listed and written in the list of the SVR, contrary to that listed in the document which I was given by the SVR; for example: Mackinovski, Mackinovski, Cankulovski, Cankulovski, Milevski, Milosevski [as interpreted]. These were mistakes in the letters.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does that mean, Mr. Popovski, relating to what you said in this document responding to the request of the Defence and your statement, saying that eight persons received compensation, while two you're unable to check? How many persons, after your additional check, received compensation in this given period of time?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: After the additional verification, we noted that 14 persons received compensation; that is to say, 13 of them were engaged from the 16th of August, and one of them only in the course of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding this omission you noted, did you gather documents which clearly speak of this omission, of this mistake, and did you inform the Defence about this?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. I got the lists which established the compensations for these persons with the orders prepared by SVR Skopje for payment and the banks where the money should be transferred; and when I came to The Hague, I brought them with me, these additional documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are these the documents, which yesterday in the course of the preparations for this testimony, you handed over to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, these are these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In additional to the verification of these individual listed 40 individuals, did you made checks of other persons; and, if so, why?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. Additionally, a request came to the ministry for check of eight additional persons, and then the logical ensuing step was to undertake this verification because the sector of finance is the instance which transfers the money;. And since Mr. Spase Filipov is not of good health and has not travelled for a long time due to health reasons, I made these additional verifications for the additional eight persons, and this is the same as regards the other 40 persons. The check was exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now look at document after tab 5, which is Exhibit 1D263, MFI.

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this document?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you have, did you act upon it?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the document with Mr. Spase Filipov.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the witness to speak up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, this is the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On two occasions, Mr. Popovski, you said that you checked the payroll and then the compensation. Where are lists and records of salaries kept?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: The records and lists for the payroll are kept in the sector for finance; that is to say, in the sector where I work. After the verification of the ID numbers, since none of these persons were on the payroll, this, in turn, is proof that that person is not employed at the MOI.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you check the compensations and who receives compensation, salary or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Lists with compensations, I checked in SVR Skopje because the persons from the list are on the SVR Skopje lists. They have a list of reservists; however, the list which is reliable is that for the compensation, in view of the fact that any engagement, regardless of the time-period, has to become compensated. If a person is not on this list, this means that the person was not engaged at all by the SVR, in this given case, SVR Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Popovski, for the first 40 persons, check the records personally, as well the records for these additionally requested eight persons?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that regarding the 40 persons you already clarified and mentioned that there had been certain mistakes, please tell me, when checking these additional eight persons, did you establish if any of these persons in the relevant time-period received any kind of compensations as engaged reserve --

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: From the second list, no person has received compensation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in view of the additional answers of the witness, I would seek to tender, together with the explanation, to tender first Exhibit 65 ter 1D1253, certified by the official of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is the statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D326, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document at tab 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is 65 ter 1D1254.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the list of persons -- the first list of persons which you checked for which you prepared a document about your understanding and for which, later, you established certain mistakes which you described in detail before this Court? Is this the list?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would seek to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D327, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document which you looked at previously, after tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is it 65 ter 1D1309.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It signed by you and submitted to the Defence on the 16th of August, 2007. Is in the document which you submitted to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would seek to tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D328, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please, look again at the document at tab 5.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is it 1D263, MFI.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the request which you personally checked, Mr. Popovski, after Spase Filipov, due to reasons you mentioned, was not able to travel?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D263, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be shown the document at tab 6. This is 1D264, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Popovski, can you confirm that the persons listed which you saw on the previous list did not receive salaries after having checked all the lists for this relevant period of time, and that these persons, as you testified, did not receive any kind of compensation for the reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: GJOKO POPOVSKI
utterances.text: Da [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would seek to tender this document into evidence as a Defence exhibit. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your answer, witness, was not recorded in the transcript. Please could you please answer, once again, whether these eight persons which you personally checked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That evidence has been given Ms. Residovic, earlier when the witness looked at it. No need to repeat it now. The document will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, his answer was not recorded in line 20, but we presume that he confirmed this as you already mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit 1D264.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. We must now adjourn, as we are over time. Sir, I'm afraid we must ask you to return on Monday at 2.15 for the continuation of your evidence. It's not possible to conclude it today in the time that we have available. We now adjourn, to resume at 2.15 Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
